questions.q: Which international organization publishes air quality guidelines that many nations use as a reference?
options: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)
questions.solution:
The WHO publishes the Global Air Quality Guidelines (2021 update), setting reference values for PM2.5, PM10, ozone and other pollutants that many countries benchmark against.
**Answer: World Health Organization (WHO)**

questions.q: The title "Zinda Pir" or "Living Saint" was attributed to:
questions.solution:
Aurangzeb, the sixth Mughal emperor, was called 'Zinda Pir' (Living Saint) for his ascetic personal habits and devotion to religious duties. (Alamgir was his regnal title.)
**Answer: Aurangzeb**

questions.q: The Chola inscription at Uttaramerur is primarily concerned with:
questions.solution:
The Uttaramerur inscription of Parantaka Chola I details the kudavolai (pot-ticket) system for electing village committees, their qualifications and duties — a landmark record of local self-government.
**Answer: Village administration**

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment granted constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions?
questions.solution:
The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992) gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions and added Part IX with the Eleventh Schedule.
**Answer: 73rd Amendment**

questions.q: Which athlete's victory marked India's inaugural gold medal moment in the Youth Olympics?
questions.solution:
Weightlifter Jeremy Lalrinnunga won India's first-ever Youth Olympics gold, lifting 274 kg in the men's 62 kg event at Buenos Aires 2018.
**Answer: Jeremy Lalrinnunga**

questions.q: Where were the 2008 Commonwealth Youth Games primarily hosted?
questions.solution:
The 2008 Commonwealth Youth Games, the inaugural edition, were hosted in Pune, India, with about 1,300 athletes from 71 nations.
**Answer: Pune**

questions.q: In which of the following shapes is the famous Sun Temple at Konark designed?
questions.solution:
The Konark Sun Temple (Odisha, 13th century, Narasimhadeva I) is built as a gigantic stone chariot of the Sun god with 24 carved wheels drawn by seven horses.
**Answer: A gigantic chariot**

questions.q: Which Indo-European style combined Gothic, Mughal, and Hindu features during the colonial era?
questions.solution:
Indo-Saracenic architecture, developed by British architects in late-19th-century India, fused Gothic, Mughal and Hindu elements — seen in buildings like the Chepauk Palace and Gateway of India.
**Answer: Indo-Saracenic**

questions.q: Which Norwegian author won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2023 for his innovative plays and prose?
questions.solution:
Norwegian novelist and playwright Jon Fosse won the 2023 Nobel Prize in Literature 'for his innovative plays and prose which give voice to the unsayable'.
**Answer: Jon Fosse**

questions.q: Which sport's terminology includes "Queen's Gambit"?
questions.solution:
'Queen's Gambit' is a classic chess opening in which White offers a pawn (d4, c4) to gain centre control.
**Answer: Chess**

questions.q: Which celebration in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana signifies the start of the harvest season and the official start of the New Year?
questions.solution:
Ugadi (Yugadi), celebrated in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka, marks the Telugu/Kannada New Year and the start of the spring harvest season in the Deccan.
**Answer: Ugadi**

questions.q: "Lezim" is a folk dance from which state?
questions.solution:
Lezim, named after the lezim (jingle-stick) dancers carry, is a vigorous folk dance of Maharashtra performed during festivals and processions.
**Answer: Maharashtra**

questions.q: What is the primary source of Kathakali's dramatic stories?
questions.solution:
Kathakali draws its plays chiefly from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and other Indian epics, rendered through mudras, music and elaborate makeup.
**Answer: Indian epics**

questions.q: Which of the following rulers founded the Nalanda University?
questions.solution:
Nalanda Mahavihara was founded by Gupta emperor Kumaragupta I (c. 427 CE) in Bihar; it grew into the ancient world's most famous Buddhist centre of learning.
**Answer: Kumaragupta I**

questions.q: The famous Chinese pilgrim, Fahien visited India during the reign of
questions.solution:
Faxian (Fahien) visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II (c. 399–414 CE) and recorded the prosperity of the Gupta empire and the state of Buddhism.
**Answer: Chandragupta II**

questions.q: Which one of these classical musicians is credited with popularizing the sitar in the global music scene?
questions.solution:
Pandit Ravi Shankar took the sitar to world audiences — through concerts abroad, collaborations (Beatles-era, with Yehudi Menuhin) and his Carnegie Hall/Monterey appearances.
**Answer: Pandit Ravi Shankar**

questions.q: Which of these is true about Bandi Chhor Divas?
options: Commemorates Guru Hargobind's release with 52 kings
It marks the martyrdom of Guru Arjan Dev during Mughal rule.
The festival involves fasting and silence throughout the day.
Celebrated only at Golden Temple without any street processions.
questions.solution:
Bandi Chhor Divas marks Guru Hargobind's release from Gwalior Fort, where he secured the freedom of 52 imprisoned kings by insisting they hold his cloak as he walked out; it coincides with Diwali at Amritsar.
**Answer: Commemorates Guru Hargobind's release with 52 kings**

questions.q: Which of the following statements about traditional and semi-classical Indian music forms are correct? 1) Kajri is sung by women in Uttar Pradesh during the monsoon, often with night-long group dancing. 2) Qawwali, introduced by Turkish Sufis, is performed only as solo singing without chorus. 3) Tappa from Punjab features rapid, jumpy notes inspired by camel riders' songs. 4) Amir Khusro helped shape Qawwali in India as a Sufi devotional form.
questions.solution:
Statement 2 is wrong: Qawwali is choral, with a lead qawwal backed by a singing party (and was shaped in India by Amir Khusro, supporting statement 4). Kajri (statement 1) and Tappa (statement 3) are correctly described, so 1, 3 and 4 are correct.
**Answer: 1, 3 and 4 only**

questions.q: Read the below statements about Indian Sports Infrastructure: 1. The Sports Authority of India was established in 1985. 2. National Sports University is located in Manipur. 3. The Army Sports Institute is based in Pune. Which of these statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement 1 is wrong: the Sports Authority of India was created in 1984, not 1985. The National Sports University is at Imphal, Manipur, and the Army Sports Institute is at Pune — so only 2 and 3 are correct.
**Answer: Only 2 and 3 are Correct**

questions.q: In 1916, two major political groups in India came together to present a united front to the British. Which organizations signed this historic agreement, known as the Lucknow Pact?
options: Indian National Congress and Swaraj Party
All-India Muslim League and Khilafat Committee
Indian National Congress and Muslim League
Hindu Mahasabha and Indian National Congress
questions.solution:
The Lucknow Pact (December 1916) was signed between the Indian National Congress and the All-India Muslim League, with Congress accepting separate electorates for Muslims.
**Answer: Indian National Congress and Muslim League**

questions.q: What was the primary focus of the 1812 House of Commons Committee before the renewal of the East India Company's Charter in 1813?
options: Judicial and police administration in India
questions.solution:
Before the Charter Act of 1813, the 1812 House of Commons Committee examined the Company's governance of conquered territories, stressing the need to improve judicial and police administration in India rather than its trade.
**Answer: Judicial and police administration in India**

questions.q: 'The God of Small Things' won the Booker Prize in which year?
questions.solution:
Arundhati Roy's debut novel 'The God of Small Things' won the Booker Prize in 1997.
**Answer: 1997**

questions.q: Who won the men's and women's singles titles at the Senior National Badminton Championships 2024 held in Bengaluru?
questions.solution:
At the 2024 Senior National Badminton Championships in Bengaluru, M. Raghu won the men's singles title and Devika Sihag the women's singles title.
**Answer: M Raghu and Devika Sihag**

questions.q: From the given renowned personalities, which one was posthumously awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 2025 in the field of Literature and Education?
questions.solution:
Writer M. T. Vasudevan Nair, who died in December 2024, was posthumously awarded the Padma Vibhushan (2025) in Literature and Education. (Khehar got PV in Public Affairs; Lakhia in Art.)
**Answer: M. T. Vasudevan Nair**

questions.q: The Himachal range includes famous hill stations and valleys such as:
questions.solution:
The Himachal (Lesser Himalayan) range contains well-known hill stations and valleys such as Kullu, Kangra and Kashmir; Munnar–Nilgiris lie in the Western Ghats/South, Ladakh–Nubra in the Trans-Himalaya.
**Answer: Kullu, Kangra, and Kashmir**

questions.q: Who has been appointed as the Chief Justice of India with effect from May 14, 2025?
questions.solution:
Justice Bhushan Ramkrishna Gavai took office as the 52nd Chief Justice of India on 14 May 2025, succeeding Justice Sanjiv Khanna.
**Answer: Shri Justice Bhushan Ramkrishna Gavai**

questions.q: - Read the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) carefully and choose the correct option: Assertion (A): The northeastern extension of the Deccan Plateau is known for distinct hill ranges like the Garo, Khasi, and Jaintia Hills. Reason (R): These hills are part of the Chotanagpur Plateau, from which they are separated by a geological fault.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true A
questions.solution:
A is true: the Garo, Khasi and Jaintia Hills form the Meghalaya Plateau, a northeastern extension of the Peninsular Plateau. R is false — they are not part of the Chotanagpur Plateau (the Meghalaya Plateau is separated from it by the Malda gap/Garo-Rajmahal gap).
**Answer: A is true, but R is false**

questions.q: According to Census 2011, which state had the lowest population density in India?
questions.solution:
Arunachal Pradesh recorded India's lowest population density in Census 2011 (about 17 persons per sq km), reflecting its mountainous, forested terrain. (Sikkim ≈ 86, Nagaland ≈ 119.)
**Answer: Arunachal Pradesh**

questions.q: Fill in the Blanks: NISAR satellite carries dual-frequency radar bands ______ and ______.
questions.solution:
NISAR, the joint ISRO–NASA radar mission, carries an L-band (NASA) and an S-band (ISRO) dual-frequency SAR — the first such dual-band imaging radar in orbit.
**Answer: L & S**

questions.q: Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are given below. Choose the correct option: Assertion (A): The death rate measures the number of deaths per 100 people in a population. Reason (R): Death rate helps track the health and mortality trends in a region.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.solution:
A is false: the crude death rate is measured per 1,000 population, not per 100. R is true — death rates are standard tools for tracking mortality and health trends.
**Answer: A is false, but R is true**

questions.q: Which four metro cities are connected by India's Golden Quadrilateral highway network?
questions.solution:
The Golden Quadrilateral links Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata, forming a 5,846-km four/six-lane expressway loop between India's four metros.
**Answer: Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata**

questions.q: Why has ISRO proposed the development of a third launch pad beyond the existing facilities at Sriharikota?
options: To serve exclusively as a data relay hub for enhancing satellite telemetry
To accommodate space tourism missions under future commercial programmes
To provide backup support in case of emergency ground failures during launches
To handle increasing launch frequency and capacity for missions involving SSLV, Gaganyaan, and commercial payloads
questions.solution:
ISRO's proposed third launch pad at Sriharikota is meant to raise launch frequency and capacity, support the NGLV/SSLV class of vehicles, Gaganyaan crewed missions and heavier commercial payloads.
**Answer: To handle increasing launch frequency and capacity for missions involving SSLV, Gaganyaan, and commercial payloads**

questions.q: Read the following statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Choose the correct option. Assertion (A): Liquid Oxygen-Methane (LOX-Meth) has been chosen as the preferred propellant combination for India's Next-Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV). Reason (R): LOX-Meth offers advantages such as cleaner combustion for engine reusability, relatively simpler propellant compared to LOX-Hydrogen, and a lower overall operational cost than kerosene due to reduced engine refurbishment.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.solution:
Both are true and R explains A: methalox engines burn cleaner (enabling reuse with less refurbishment), simplify tank/propellant handling compared to LOX-hydrogen, and cut operational cost — exactly why ISRO chose LOX-methane for the NGLV.
**Answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**

questions.q: Which of the following biomolecules is most abundant in plant cell walls?
questions.solution:
Cellulose, a structural polysaccharide of glucose chains, makes up the bulk of plant cell walls (with hemicellulose, pectin and lignin as lesser/secondary components).
**Answer: Cellulose**

questions.q: Given four enzymes: 1. DNA polymerase 2. Ligase 3. Helicase 4. Peptidase. Which are directly involved in DNA replication?
questions.solution:
DNA replication directly needs helicase (unwinds the double helix), DNA polymerase (synthesises new strands) and ligase (joins Okazaki fragments). Peptidase digests proteins, so 1, 2 and 3 are involved.
**Answer: 1, 2 and 3**

questions.q: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita(BNSS) allows for trials to proceed in the absence of the accused in certain circumstances. This provision applies specifically to:
options: Any accused person who fails to appear.
Accused persons who are gravely ill.
questions.solution:
Under the BNSS, trial and even judgment can proceed in the absence of an accused who is a proclaimed offender absconding to evade trial (provisions on proclamation and trials in absentia).
**Answer: Proclaimed offenders who abscond.**

questions.q: What is the maximum period of imprisonment that can be given in a summary trial under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, irrespective of the punishment specified for the offence?
questions.solution:
In summary trials under the BNSS, the court cannot pass a sentence of imprisonment exceeding three months, irrespective of the offence's prescribed punishment.
**Answer: 3 months**

questions.q: e-NAM is primarily aimed at which of the following?
questions.solution:
e-NAM (National Agriculture Market) is a pan-India electronic trading portal that networks APMC mandis into a single national digital market for farm produce.
**Answer: National digital market**

questions.q: Consider the following statements about Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) scheme: Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Both are correct: the NBS scheme pays fixed per-kg subsidies on nitrogen (N), phosphate (P), potash (K) and sulphur (S) in non-urea fertilizers, and also includes freight assistance so rates are uniform across states.
**Answer: Both 1 and 2**

questions.q: The Global Liveability Index 2025, a form of Global Cities Index, is published by which organization?
questions.solution:
The Global Liveability Index, ranking cities on stability, healthcare, culture/environment, education and infrastructure, is published annually by the EIU (Economist Intelligence Unit).
**Answer: EIU**

questions.q: Mario de Miranda, known for his cartoons and sketches, hailed from which Indian state?
questions.solution:
Cartoonist Mario de Miranda (Mario Miranda), famous for his Goan village scenes and Mumbai life sketches and a Padma Vibhushan recipient, hailed from Goa.
**Answer: Goa**

questions.q: What is the impact of PSU disinvestment on the government's financial structure?
options: It increases the government's earnings permanently
It does not affect finances at all
questions.solution:
Disinvestment is a non-debt capital receipt earned by selling government equity in PSUs — it reduces the government's financial assets (its ownership stake) rather than raising liabilities.
**Answer: It reduces government's financial assets**

questions.q: Consider the following statements and choose the correct option: Statement 1: A surplus on the current account indicates that the country is lending to the rest of the world. Statement 2: A current account is said to be in balance when payments exceed receipts,
options: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct
Neither Statement 1 nor Statement 2 is correct
questions.solution:
Only Statement 1 is correct: a current account surplus means a country saves more than it invests domestically and is a net lender to the world. Statement 2 is wrong — balance means payments equal receipts, not that payments exceed them.
**Answer: Only Statement 1 is correct**

questions.q: Which year marked the beginning of India's First Five-Year Plan?
questions.solution:
India's First Five-Year Plan was launched in 1951 (1951–56), focused on agriculture, irrigation and the Harrod-Domar growth model.
**Answer: 1951**

questions.q: Read the following statements and mark the correct option: Assertion (A): Subramaniya Siva edited the nationalist journal 'Gnanabhanu' in Tamil Nadu. Reason (R): He was the first Indian to be arrested under the Rowlatt Act.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.solution:
A is true: Subramaniya Siva edited the Tamil nationalist journal 'Gnanabhanu'. R is false — he was arrested in the Tirunelveli conspiracy case (1908), well before the Rowlatt Act (1919); the first arrest under the Rowlatt Act is not attributed to him.
**Answer: A is true, but R is false.**

questions.q: Which of the following pairs correctly represent light industries?
questions.solution:
Light industries use light raw materials and produce small consumer goods — knitting needles and electric bulbs are classic examples; shipbuilding, automobiles and oil are heavy industries.
**Answer: Knitting needles and Electric bulbs**

questions.q: Read the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) carefully and choose the correct option. Assertion (A): The Green Revolution led to regional imbalances in agricultural growth. Reason (R): HYV technology and irrigation facilities were initially available only in select states.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.solution:
Both are true and R explains A: HYV seeds, fertilizers and assured irrigation were first available only in Punjab, Haryana and western UP, so the Green Revolution's gains concentrated there and created regional imbalance.
**Answer: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.**

questions.q: Read the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) carefully and choose the correct option. Assertion (A): The Minimum Needs Programme (MNP) was introduced in the Fifth Plan. Reason (R): It targeted improvement in quality of life through education, health, and drinking water.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.solution:
Both are true and R explains A: the Minimum Needs Programme of the Fifth Plan aimed to raise living standards by providing basic needs — elementary education, health, drinking water, nutrition and rural roads.
**Answer: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.**

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the Aravalli Green Wall Project: 1. It is intended to check desertification across Western India. 2. The project is being implemented in four Indian states. 3. It aims to construct eco-sensitive highways along forest corridors.
questions.solution:
Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Aravalli Green Wall Project targets 5-km-wide, 1,400-km-long greening of the Aravalli range across four states (Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana, Delhi) to check desertification eastward from the Thar; it is about afforestation, not eco-sensitive highways (3 is wrong).
**Answer: Only 1 and 2 are correct**

questions.q: Which of the following was not a goal of 1991 economic reforms?
questions.solution:
The 1991 New Economic Policy aimed at competitiveness, foreign investment and fiscal discipline through liberalisation — expanding public sector control is the opposite (disinvestment and delicensing shrank the PSUs' role).
**Answer: Expand public sector control**
